clue.text: Send lifers to stir for solitary

indicators.note: to stir is to mix up, so the letters of these two words are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A prisoner recommends sending lifers off to solitary confinement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stir' is slang for prison, which fits the lifers and solitary, but here it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with no companions is solitary, alone in the world without allies.

clue.text: Newspaper includes excellent feature

indicators.note: the newspaper's letters contain the next piece, so it sits inside them

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times
ace means excellent

explanation.surface: A newspaper runs an excellent feature article.
explanation.definitionFit: A facet is one aspect or characteristic, a synonym of feature in the sense of trait.

clue.text: Misanthrope's lie heard in tax haven

indicators.note: heard signals that the words are spoken, so the spoken phrase gives the entry's sound

parts.note: a hater of people would be lying in saying 'I love man'

explanation.surface: A people-hater tells a fib while living in an offshore tax haven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I love man' said quickly, as 'I-lo'-man', sounds like 'Isle o' Man'. The Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea, is a self-governing British Crown dependency known for low taxes.
explanation.definitionFit: The island has low income tax and no capital gains tax, so it is widely described as an offshore haven.

clue.text: Balt's home, grand property for temporary occupants?

parts.note: a Lett is a Latvian, one of the Baltic peoples
in means at home
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A Latvian's house is a grand property, rented out to short-term tenants.
explanation.definitionFit: A let property is rented to tenants for a fixed spell, and Britons call such a place a letting.

clue.text: Short odds on horse displaying vivacity

parts.note: SP is short for starting price, the odds at the start of a race
Arkle was a famous Irish steeplechaser, three-time Cheltenham Gold Cup winner

explanation.surface: Backing a horse at short odds shows liveliness in the punter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short odds' looks like a betting term meaning a strong favourite, but 'Short' asks for an abbreviation of 'odds'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparkle is liveliness and brilliance of manner, a synonym of vivacity.

clue.text: State time for embarkation if there's delay

indicators.note: something embarked goes on board, so the time letter boards, going inside the other word

parts.note: to state is to say

explanation.surface: Officials announce a time for passengers to board a delayed ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay is a postponement, as in a stay of execution, so it means a delay.

clue.text: Drums making rhythmical pattern entertaining bishop

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to hold them within, so the pattern word surrounds the next piece

parts.note: a tala is a rhythmic cycle in Indian classical music
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Drummers tap out a rhythm to amuse a visiting bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: The tabla is a pair of Indian hand drums, so the plural noun fits the set.

clue.text: Sailors? See 'em beginning to croon shanty when drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests something reeling and disordered, so these letters are tossed into a new order
the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Sailors sing sea shanties loudly once they have had a few drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is a link pointing at the pieces: EM, the C that begins 'croon', and SHANTY are jumbled together by 'when drunk'.
explanation.definitionFit: People who sail yachts are a kind of sailor, hence the question mark marking an example.

clue.text: Criminal little clique in which moralist's no good

indicators.note: the clique contains the next piece, which sits inside it

parts.note: a cult is a small exclusive group

indicators.note: no good means the G for good is dropped

parts.note: a prig is a smug moralist

explanation.surface: A small gang of crooks harbours a moralist who has gone bad.
explanation.definitionFit: A culprit is the person guilty of an offence, a noun synonym of criminal.

clue.text: "Be calm!" ordered to keep one still

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so the rearranged letters hold the next piece inside
ordered here means arranged, so the letters are put into a new sequence

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone is told to stay calm and keep perfectly still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges BECALM; 'to keep' puts I inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: An alembic is an old distilling apparatus, so it is a kind of still.

clue.text: Bit of wood maybe not thin enough, needing pressure to get in

indicators.note: the pressure letter gets in, going inside the phrase

parts.note: too thick means not thin enough
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A sliver of wood that is too thick needs pushing to fit in.
explanation.definitionFit: A toothpick is a small sliver, usually of wood, an example of a bit of wood, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Lots of land men covered in farm vehicle

indicators.note: covered here means hidden from view, so the men's letters disappear from the vehicle word

parts.note: a tractor is the standard farm vehicle
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Farm workers ride under cover in a tractor across wide acres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered' looks like it should put the men inside something; here it means hidden from sight, so the men drop out of the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A tract is a large expanse of land or water.

clue.text: Area of grassland where two rivers meet

parts.note: the Cam flows through Cambridge
the Po is Italy's longest river

explanation.surface: Meadows lie at the confluence of two rivers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two rivers' supplies both pieces: the Cam and the Po.
explanation.definitionFit: A campo is a grassy plain in South America, especially Brazil.

clue.text: Birds in capital crossing a river

indicators.note: the capital stretches across the other pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: Caracas is the capital of Venezuela
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Birds fly over a river in a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Caracaras are South American birds of prey of the falcon family.

clue.text: Dress circles never circling theatre? Only a bit of it

definitions.text: theatre? Only a bit of it

indicators.note: the dress word goes round the next piece, enclosing it

parts.note: to groom is to dress or tidy, as of a horse or hair

indicators.note: circling means turning round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: ne'er is the poetic contraction of never

explanation.surface: A theatre's dress circle has never been surrounded by spectators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dress circles' looks like the theatre balcony, and that steers you away from reading 'Dress' as a verb for tidying up.
explanation.definitionFit: The green room is the backstage lounge where performers wait, only one part of a theatre.

clue.text: Obvious way for collecting runs?

parts.note: overt means open and obvious

indicators.note: the way word collects the runs letter, taking it inside

parts.note: how means the way something is done
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricket question asks about the plainest way to pile up runs.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an overthrow is a fielder's throw that beats the stumps and lets the batters run extra, an easy gift of runs.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild return by a fielder gives batters extra runs, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: What makes tenor sing badly, producing mechanical sounds?

indicators.note: singing badly means getting the notes out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something makes a tenor sing off-key, producing robotic noises.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringtones are the electronic sounds a phone plays on an incoming call.

clue.text: Singer is ace in Portuguese tourist centre

indicators.note: the ace letter goes inside the town's name

parts.note: Sintra is a palace town near Lisbon, popular with tourists
A is the card abbreviation for ace

explanation.surface: A singer is a big hit in a Portuguese holiday town.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Sinatra was the American crooner, an example of a singer.

clue.text: Asian bar mentioned in marketing ploy

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken, so these words give the entry by their sound

parts.note: a Thai inn would be an Asian drinking place

explanation.surface: An Asian bar gets a plug as part of a sales promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie-in is a product linked to a film or book to promote both, a marketing device.

clue.text: Poet's worry about short line

definitions.note: the possessive reads as poet is, so the poet's name is the answer

indicators.note: the worry word goes about the next piece, surrounding it

parts.note: care means worry
L is short for line

explanation.surface: A poet frets over a line that falls short.
explanation.walkthrough: John Clare was the English nature poet of Northamptonshire.
explanation.definitionFit: John Clare was a nineteenth-century English rural poet.

clue.text: Dismay in prayer with no end to vielence

indicators.note: no means the following letter is left out

parts.note: an appeal is an earnest request or prayer

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: People pray in dismay for violence to cease.
explanation.walkthrough: The print spells the last word 'vielence', a typo for violence; its last letter is E either way, which comes out of APPEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal is to fill with horror, a verb synonym of dismay.

clue.text: Effortful study leads to a degree in education

parts.note: to con is to study
Cert Ed is a Certificate in Education, a teaching qualification

explanation.surface: Diligent study leads to a teaching qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: A concerted effort is a determined one, so the word means effortful.

clue.text: Common people: duke has upset a few

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so in a down entry the word is read backwards

parts.note: some means a few

explanation.surface: A duke annoys a handful of commoners.
explanation.definitionFit: Demos is the Greek word for the populace, the common people.

clue.text: Gripped by fear, I posted reply

indicators.note: the words grip the answer, holding it inside their run of letters

explanation.surface: In a panic, I sent off my response.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick retort, a sharp reply.

clue.text: Three characters in uniform on public transport?

indicators.note: the uniform word goes inside the transport word

parts.note: a tram is a form of public transport
a rig is an outfit or uniform

explanation.surface: Three people in uniform ride a tram.
explanation.definitionFit: A trigram is a group of three letters or characters.

clue.text: Mass of rock, yet not tons

indicators.note: not means the tons letter is left out

parts.note: still means yet

explanation.surface: A great mass of rock, yet not tons in weight.
explanation.definitionFit: In geology a sill is a sheet of igneous rock intruded between strata.

clue.text: Collapses in gentle hills when on holiday

indicators.note: the hills come after, on top of, the holiday word

parts.note: a break is a holiday
downs are rolling chalk hills of southern England

explanation.surface: Walkers collapse on the gentle hills while away on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Breakdowns are failures or collapses, mechanical or mental.
